podcast.title: Britpop Launchpad
podcast.body: Released on April 25, 1994, this album was instrumental in launching Britpop. It was a direct result of Damon Albarn's determination to make British music distinct again after a difficult US tour and helped Britpop to truly take off. "The result was a 1994 album called Park Live and from the time of its release on April 25, 1994, Britpop was pretty much off and running."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock: Chapter 12

podcast.title: Career-Altering Album
podcast.body: Released on April 25, 1994, just 17 days after Kurt Cobain's death, *Park Life* was a "career altering and game-changing" album for Blur, capitalizing on the vacuum left by grunge's decline. The album had a multi-generational appeal due to its "Englishness," embraced by both "indie hipsters to mums and dads." "The 17 days after Kurt died, Blur released a career altering and game-changing, not to mention a very British album called Park Life."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall of Britpop

podcast.title: Game-Changing Album
podcast.body: Released on April 25, 1994, just 17 days after Kurt Cobain's death, this album was a career-altering and game-changing release for Blur, noted for its distinctly British character. Its "Englishness" gave it a multi-generational appeal, embraced by indie hipsters, mums, and dads alike, and it was at its peak when Oasis's *Definitely Maybe* was released. "Right place, right time, right album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
